newsitem.title: USA: Counsel calls for Gingrich fine, reprimand -report.
newsitem.headline: Counsel calls for Gingrich fine, reprimand -report.

text.p: The special counsel in the ethics case involving House Speaker Newt Gingrich will recommend a heavy fine and referral of the case to the Justice Department, the New York Times reported Friday.
Counsel James Cole worked on his report to the committee through the night Thursday and planned to present it to the committee later Friday.
In addition, the Baltimore Sun Friday reported that sources close to the investigation said Cole recommended a reprimand and a fine of more than $100,000.
Cole also recommended that the matter be referred to the Justice Department for possible criminal prosecution, legislative aides told the Sun and Times.
Quoting House aides from both parties, the Times said Cole would be very critical of the speaker, whose ethical problems have consumed the nation's capitol for the past several weeks.
The committee was expected to meet in closed session later in the morning, with the possibility of open meetings still up in the air.
The Times said the committee had been ready to meet in open session Friday afternoon but Republicans backed off after finding out Cole's report would be so critical.

Gingrich has admitted to bringing discredit to the House by giving the committee untrue information and not seeking proper legal assistance in setting up tax-free groups to help with a college course he taught.
The ethics committee is considering what punishment to recommend to the full House, which has scheduled a vote on the matter Tuesday.
